name: Bare Role Construction
pattern: NP[Det:absent + Nom[Head:singular count role noun]], in a licensed role slot

entry.name: Bare Role Construction
entry.pattern: NP[Det:absent + Nom[Head:singular count role noun]], in a licensed role slot

dimensions.form: A singular count nominal, optionally modified, with no determiner
dimensions.meaning: Presents an office, assignment, or role that can be held or taken on
dimensions.function: Subject- or object-oriented predicative, complement of a preposition in a licensed frame, or ascriptive supplement
dimensions.distribution: Available in particular role-denoting senses and constructions. Ordinary referential subject and object positions generally require a determiner with the same singular count noun.

1.definition: Ascribes an office or institutional role, or gives the content of an office expression.
1.details: The same nominal can follow be, become, remain, appoint, or elect when the verb licenses a predicative complement. It can also occur with as and in role of or position of, in a matrix-licensed except phrase, or as an ascriptive supplement. In an appointment construction the direct object identifies the appointee and the bare NP gives the office.

examples.form: They appointed Lee [treasurer of the club].
examples.note: Constructed object-oriented predicative. In They questioned the treasurer of the club, the article-marked NP instead identifies the person questioned.
Constructed prepositional frame. Compare Lee applied for the position [of treasurer]. Both retain a bare role nominal.

examples.form: Faatulu was named [co-captain] along with fellow junior Jamie Peck.
examples.note: The sports report explicitly names two holders of the role.

grounds.locator: Paragraph beginning As one of the few upperclassmen

examples.note: Constructed after CGEL’s comparison. Lee is the secretary of the club can also specify the incumbent in answer to Who is the secretary?
The except phrase picks out a role from the alternatives made available by the matrix clause.

examples.form: Wilson, [Secretary to the Cabinet], had informed the Prime Minister immediately.
examples.note: Ascriptive supplement. The bare NP cannot replace Wilson as the referential subject.

2.definition: Ascribes a professional assignment construed as a post.
2.details: A workplace can make a particular assignment available for the construction. The availability of a bare form is sensitive to lexical choice and how a job title is used in the institution.

examples.form: They appointed Lee [lead counsel] for the appeal.
examples.note: Constructed. Lead counsel specifies the assignment.
Constructed comparison. In ordinary standard usage, became lawyer is degraded on the professional-class reading.

3.definition: Ascribes a relational or ceremonial role in a licensed frame.
3.details: A following relational dependent can specify whom the role is held in relation to. This use is limited to independently available role expressions. It is distinct from using a kin term as a form of address or as a standing name. Holding a kin role doesn't confer the kin term as a designation: Schneider and Homans report that when a child is reared from infancy by an aunt playing a maternal role, she “is still not called ‘mother’” (1955: 1203).

examples.form: They asked Lee to be [godfather to their son].
examples.note: Constructed relational example. The to-phrase supplies the other participant.

examples.form: There can likewise be only one person who is [father of the student I have in mind].
examples.note: CGEL’s own prose, discussing the identifiability of the father of the student; the sentence's opening In [2ii] is omitted. A kin noun heads the bare predicative, and of the student gives the relatum.

Constructed. A single kin noun, with the to-phrase giving the relatum. Kin nouns under this meaning are an adjudication (Brett, 2026-11-19): CGEL lists kin or similar relations separately from offices or roles (Ch. 4 §5.5.1(e)).

constraints.description: A bare role NP can describe the subject or object. It does not ordinarily occupy the subject or object position as a referential expression for the roleholder.
The choice of noun and context must support a role reading. Predicative function alone does not license removal of the article from become a miser or become a teacher.

The role can have multiple holders. A counterpart with an overt determiner can also ascribe a role, as in became a co-captain or remained our captain. With be, a counterpart with the can additionally identify the contextually relevant incumbent.

relatedConstructions.notes: This is one use of a determinerless NP headed by a nominal.
A bare role NP can ascribe a post to the subject.
In the appointment frame the predicand is realized as object.
A bare role NP can be the predicative complement of as or a complement of selected of or except.
Compare became co-captain and became a co-captain. Both can ascribe the same post.
Compare remained captain and remained our captain. The determiner adds a relation to the speaker’s group. With be, the captain can also give a specifying reading.
Compare Lee is secretary of the club and Lee is the secretary of the club. The latter can answer Who is the secretary?
Wilson, Secretary to the Cabinet shares the supplement packaging. Its bare supplement cannot replace Wilson as subject, which is CGEL’s diagnostic against apposition here.
Both license bare singular count NPs. Compare remained treasurer with went to school. The licensed slots and interpretations differ.
Role nouns can also occur bare as paired endpoints, as in from teacher to pupil. The pairing licenses a source–goal interpretation.
Compare Chair, may I respond? with Lee remained chair. The role noun serves as a form of address in the first example and a predicative in the second.

Both are determinerless singular NPs whose definite interpretation is relative to a domain, an organisation for treasurer and a household for Mom. Function distinguishes them: a bare role NP is predicative or in a licensed frame (Lee remained treasurer), while a strong proper name is a referential argument (Mom called; compare CGEL’s ∗I’m told treasurer strongly supports this proposal, p. 409). Inserting the keeps the ascription in Henry became the treasurer (p. 409) but loses the name in The mom called (constructed). A role form used as a standing name independently licenses referential argument uses.

grounds.locator: Ch. 4 §5.1 [5]; Ch. 5 §8.5 [19], p. 409; Ch. 7, pp. 637–638, predicative complements of as; Ch. 15 §5, [22ii]
grounds.note: Documents verbal, prepositional, and ascriptive supplementary uses and contrasts referential object uses.

grounds.locator: Ch. 4 §5.5.1(e), contrast with secretary of the bushwalking club; Ch. 5 §8.5 [19], p. 409
grounds.note: The role ascription and the identifying interpretation differ. Chapter 5 gives the stronger replacement claim.
Kin nouns in relational predicatives (father of the student) are instances of meaning 3; kin terms used as names (Dad called) are not, and belong to strong-proper-name-001.
An aunt who raises a child in a maternal role isn't thereby called mother: the role and the designation come apart.

known_boundary_items: Dad called, but Sam answered (constructed). Dad identifies a person as subject when the family uses it as a name: an instance of strong-proper-name-001, not of this construction.

Captain called, said of Lee, a former captain the team still calls Captain, while Sam holds the post (constructed). Captain identifies Lee, the captain identifies Sam, and Lee is captain is false: the designation outlasts the tenure, so the referential use belongs to strong-proper-name-001, not to this construction.

projection.target: In ordinary standard English, with a reading that ascribes an assignment or gives its content, a nominal such as treasurer can remain bare in She stayed treasurer, They appointed her treasurer, and As treasurer, she signed. Reuse as a stand-alone referential object, as in They questioned the treasurer, normally calls for a determiner. The same bare office ascription can apply to more than one holder.
projection.evidence: CGEL compares the same noun in predicative and object positions and documents the prepositional and supplementary uses. The Arizona State report documents shared tenure. Whether a counterpart with the preserves the bare reading depends on the frame and context.

curious.title: Jobs and roles without "the" or "a"
curious.summary: Words like treasurer or captain can describe the role someone holds without a word like the or a in front.
curious.body:
Normally a word like treasurer needs company: we say the treasurer or a treasurer. But in some sentences it stands alone. They appointed Lee treasurer. Lee served as treasurer. Here the word doesn't point to a particular person. It says what role Lee has.

Compare They questioned the treasurer. That sentence is about a person, so it normally needs the. The bare version works where a role is being given or described. The role can also have more than one holder, as when two people are named co-captain.

examples.text: They appointed Lee [treasurer of the club].
Faatulu was named [co-captain] along with fellow junior Jamie Peck.

curious.try: Say "They appointed her treasurer" and "They questioned the treasurer." In which sentence does treasurer name a role, and in which does it point at a person?

teacher.summary: Explains why role nouns such as treasurer can lack a determiner in predicative and some prepositional frames.
teacher.explain: A singular count noun that names an office or post can appear with no determiner when the sentence ascribes the role to someone: after be, become, remain, appoint or elect, after as, after role of or position of, in an except phrase licensed by the main clause, or as an ascriptive supplement (Wilson, Secretary to the Cabinet, ...). The bare NP describes the subject or object. It doesn't normally stand as a referential subject or object for the role-holder, where a determiner is needed (They questioned the treasurer). The noun and context must support a role reading: the article stays in become a teacher. A version with the or a can also ascribe a role (became a co-captain), and with be, the secretary of the club can identify the current holder, answering Who is the secretary?
teacher.terms: Predicative complement: an NP such as treasurer in She stayed treasurer or They appointed her treasurer, which describes the subject or object. This dictionary treats this as a licensed use of a determinerless NP.

examples.text: They appointed Lee [treasurer of the club].
Wilson, [Secretary to the Cabinet], had informed the Prime Minister immediately.

contrasts.text: Lee is secretary of the club.
Lee is the secretary of the club.
contrasts.note: Can also answer Who is the secretary?

contrasts.text: I'm told treasurer strongly supports this proposal.
contrasts.note: A bare role noun doesn't work as a referential subject here.

watch_for: A learner might assume any job noun can go without an article after become, when the choice depends on the noun and how the job title is used.
A learner might use a bare role noun as the subject for a particular person, as in I'm told treasurer strongly supports this proposal.
teacher.activity: Give students two columns of frames (appointed Lee ___, they questioned ___, served as ___, I spoke to ___). Students fill each with treasurer or the treasurer and explain which frames ascribe a role and which identify a person.
